read_scope.notes: Read all extracted manuscript text, including references and Appendices A–G, and visually inspected all 22 rendered PDF pages. Inspected Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–12 at readable scale. Consulted frozen paper.tex and specificity_results.tex to resolve wording, source locations and the abstract; the abstract contains 151 whitespace-delimited words. Technical appendices were treated as optional depth when judging the main narrative. Used only the fixed rubric and supplied round_32 snapshot; no other reviews, previous drafts or evaluation records were consulted.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise English with concrete verbs and generally manageable sentences. The distinction between a reference-aligned response and total error is maintained consistently from the Introduction through the results. Qualifications normally sit beside the claims they limit, especially the independence assumptions on p. 5 and retrospective calibration on p. 9. Local opportunities remain in the compressed magnitude/cosine sentence in Section 5.2 and the repeated closing recap; these are refinements rather than recurrent comprehension problems.
score_reasons.structure: The paper moves coherently from the motivating Monet–Sisley comparison to experimental arms, feature interpretation, intuitive score definitions, declared results and retrospective explanations. Section 4.1 gives the reader a usable interpretation before Equations 1–3. Sections 5.3–5.5 visibly distinguish pair diagnostics, calibration and reference sensitivity from the prespecified comparisons. Detailed identities, coverage simulations and earlier cohorts are appropriately optional appendices. The Discussion and Conclusion partly duplicate their synthesis, leaving a small opportunity to tighten the ending.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The abstract is standalone and within its limit; the six clauses, two repeats, four-painter reference target and 1,008-image design can be understood without repository access. Table 1 translates features into ordinary visual properties, the lightness example makes centering concrete, and the no-distinction/exact/doubled examples explain D unusually well. Tables 2 and 4 make direction, mismatch and calibration interpretable, while captions distinguish projected geometry from all-feature scores. Only the shared-response magnitude and direction comparison in Section 5.2 remains more compressed than the surrounding explanations.
score_reasons.engagement: A consequential evaluation question is developed through concrete, inspectable examples rather than a model leaderboard alone. Figure 1 permits direct comparison across clauses, Figure 2 makes the labeled geometry visible, and Figure 3 rewards inspection by exposing uneven pair responses. The Nano Banana/FLUX scene-averaging reversal and GPT Image 2 calibration result explain what the metric choices reveal. The ending repeats several already well-established conclusions, slightly reducing the final narrative momentum.

strengths: Section 4.1, p. 5, builds intuition with the .325 versus .254 lightness gap and three idealized generators before introducing notation. This makes both the reference target and D = 1 benchmark recoverable by a new reader.

Sections 5.1 and 5.4 use actual numerical contrasts to distinguish alignment, total mismatch, scene consistency and contrast magnitude, rather than treating stronger responses or a lower point estimate as universally better.

Figures 1–3 and their captions provide complementary visual evidence: recognizable prompt changes, labeled reference/generated geometry, and all-feature pair estimates. Main figures and tables are legible and consistently labeled.

The primary versus retrospective hierarchy is explicit. In particular, Section 5.5 and Table 5 show exactly which adjusted intervals change after source correction without promoting the new GPT Image 1 comparison to a confirmatory finding.

The scope is bounded throughout to digital reference contrasts. The paper explains why source handling, subject mixtures, repeat assumptions and feature geometry limit interpretation without demanding that optional appendix derivations carry the main explanation.

findings.issue: The final paragraph compresses squared-magnitude ratios and cosines into one numerical clause. The ratio numerator is only implicit, and the reader has to unpack strength and direction together immediately after learning the shared-change percentage.
findings.reader_effect: A reader can follow the 82.5–95.7% result yet hesitate over what the 1.96–4.14 range adds, or read it too quickly as an ordinary amplitude multiplier. This is a localized loss of interpretability in an otherwise well-explained result.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the paragraph at comparable or shorter length with: “Relative to artist-free output, the average named shift points broadly in the generic-painting direction (cosine .689–.930; 1 is parallel) and has 1.96–4.14 times its squared magnitude. Both estimates use scene averages (Appendix B).” This keeps the existing evidence and makes the denominator and distinction explicit.

findings.location: Discussion and Conclusion, p. 10; paper.tex lines 310–348
findings.issue: The short Discussion already synthesizes the weak Monet–Sisley response, the distinction between estimates and resolved comparisons, and the separate effects of averaging and calibration. The Conclusion then recaps most of the results once more, including the reference-correction ordering.
findings.reader_effect: The final page loses some momentum through repetition after the reader has already been given a clear interpretation. This does not obscure the findings, but the ending could be more economical.
findings.suggested_change: Shorten the Conclusion to two or three sentences retaining the shared-response finding, the positive-alignment/no-established-benchmark-advantage distinction, and the final distinction between detecting a name response and matching painter differences. Keep calibration and source-correction specifics in Sections 5.4–5.5 and the Discussion, where their evidence is already explained. No additional material or pages are needed.

summary: Excellent communication of a bounded digital-reference comparison. The main text stands on its own, the figures support the argument, and uncertainty and retrospective status are handled carefully. Only localized wording and closing-pacing refinements remain; no new experiments or broader validation are needed to address them.
